rationale.conceptual: Building a feed-forward ANN with one hidden layer of 8 neurons, sigmoid activation, and backpropagation is a classic textbook exercise in machine learning. The architecture and training are standard, with no custom or novel methodological complexity. The problem is a straightforward regression on a predetermined set of 8 input features.
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of three trivial steps: loading a provided CSV, normalizing features, training a tiny model, and outputting a predictions CSV. No multi-tool orchestration, no external data acquisition, and no fragile dependencies beyond standard Python libraries. It is a single-script pipeline.

difficulty.reasoning: The task is to reproduce a simple feed-forward ANN QSAR model on a tiny dataset of 61 cocrystals. The method is a textbook neural network with one hidden layer, sigmoid activation, and backpropagation—no novel algorithmic or conceptual challenges. The pipeline is a short sequence of loading data, normalizing, training, and predicting; all data is supplied. No GPU or significant resources are needed. The work is squarely in the domain of chemoinformatics.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The dataset contains only 61 instances with 8 features. Training an 8-neuron hidden layer ANN on such data is trivial and completes in seconds on a CPU, using negligible memory (<0.1 GB) and no GPU.
